summary: A black, chaptered long-read about Otto Baumberger's 1920s–30s poster lettering, the source of GT Walsheim. Every chapter is a stacked full-screen 'slide' that peels away to uncover the next, and almost everything responds to pointer position: posters swap to their sketches or 2017 animations, and display samples step through the eight weights or flip alternates on and off as the pointer crosses invisible hover zones.

instances.look: A centred four-line quote from Baumberger, “I never properly learned typography, I just draw letters for my posters.”, set huge in white GT Walsheim Medium on black, tiny attribution below; 'TRY BUY PDF' in tiny caps at the top-left
instances.ux: Moving the pointer left to right across the quote steps it through the 8 weights (Ultra Light → Ultra Bold); a small dot and a style-name label ('GT Walsheim Medium') show the current stop. Fixed TRY / BUY / PDF links stay in the top-left corner on every screen
instances.learn: Let the source speak first: the designer's quote set in the font is both the pitch and the specimen, and pointer position turns it into a weight scrubber with no visible UI

reconstruction.layout: Full-viewport black slide; quote centred, ~1130px wide, 4 lines, starting ~170px from the top; attribution centred ~40px below; the large-text intro follows after ~150px. Fixed nav at x=20, y=20: three 10px links
reconstruction.typography: Quote ~110px GT Walsheim Medium (font-feature-settings kern, liga, ss01 0), leading ~1.15, sentence case, centred, curly quotes; attribution ~12px Medium; nav 10px Medium uppercase, tracked
reconstruction.behaviour: Loader first: white, then black screen with a spinning G-shaped icon and 'Loading all the things. Thank you for your patience.' (~5s). On the quote, 8 invisible absolutely positioned hover zones (12.5% wide each) map to 8 font-family swaps (gt-walsheim-ultra-light … ultra-bold); an index ball slides to the zone and the descriptor label updates; leaving restores the default (Medium)
reconstruction.content: A real quote from Otto Baumberger with attribution 'Swiss poster artist Otto Baumberger'
reconstruction.assets: none for the hero itself; loader icon (rotating G)
